bridge.title: Four things I noticed

beats.title: 14.9K followers. Your full mentorship is $80.
beats.text: Every video ends with the same two links: your trade setups for $25 and the full trading mentorship for $80, both straight into Discord. That works for people who want your setups. It leaves nothing for the traders who want you in their corner while they go through a challenge.

beats.title: 2,400 people in Team Take Profits.
beats.text: Another 345 are in TTP Setups, and you've posted 15 YouTube videos in 18 days documenting your $200K challenge trade by trade, losses included. The people watching you get $2,000 from passing are exactly the ones stuck in their own challenge.

beats.title: Every link is a Discord invite.
beats.text: Your bio, your Instagram link and every YouTube description go straight into a Discord server. There's no page that explains the mentorship, no application, and no conversation before someone joins. The traders who'd pay for real help never get asked what they need.

stats.label: Discord invites, no page in between

beats.title: “I'm still passing my own challenge.” That's the pitch.
beats.text: You don't sell perfect trades, you show the process: the rules, the mistakes, the trade you should have skipped. That's what someone stuck in their own challenge wants to see. The $25 setups and the $80 mentorship stay. The one-on-one mentorship sits on top, for the few who want you next to them.
beats.quote: “No pretending every trade is perfect. The goal is to show what trading actually looks like while becoming a better trader one decision at a time.”

bridge.closing: So instead of explaining it, I built it. The page, the application, the emails and the ads, all below.

cards.body: The challenge is going well. You keep trading anyway, and the profit is gone by the end of the day.

cards.title: You break your own rules
cards.body: You know your plan. One bad trade later, you're revenge trading and the plan is gone.

cards.title: The firm's rules catch you out
cards.body: Daily drawdown, max loss, minimum days. One rule you didn't read closely ends the challenge.

mechanism.title: Plan. Execute. Repeat.
mechanism.body: Passing a challenge isn't about one big trade. You plan the session before it starts, size every trade so one loss can't end the challenge, take only the trades in the plan, and review every one. In the mentorship, Jay goes through your challenge with you until that process is yours.

preCallEmails.subject: You're booked: here's what happens next
preCallEmails.body:
Hey {{first_name}},

Your call is booked for {{call_time}}. The link is in your calendar invite.

Before we talk:
1. Keep the time free.
2. If you're in a challenge, have your account rules and your last few trades ready.

One note: nobody on my team will ever ask you to pay through a DM. Payments only happen through the official links from this email address.

Talk soon,
Jay

preCallEmails.subject: Why most traders fail prop firms
preCallEmails.body:
Hey {{first_name}},

Most traders don't fail a challenge because their strategy is bad. They fail because they keep trading after a good day, or they break their own rule after a bad one.

I've done both on camera.

The mentorship is built on one process: plan the session, size every trade so one loss can't end the challenge, take only the planned trades, review every one.

On the call we'll look at where your process breaks today.

Jay

preCallEmails.subject: "I'm already in the Discord"
preCallEmails.previewText: Then you know how I trade
preCallEmails.body:
Hey {{first_name}},

Good. Then you've seen the setups and how I trade them.

The mentorship is for when watching isn't enough anymore: one-on-one reviews of your own trades, and a plan built around your firm's rules, so you know exactly where your challenge goes wrong.

If you're not sure you need it, ask on the call. We'll tell you honestly.

Jay

preCallEmails.subject: What we'll cover on the call
preCallEmails.body:
Hey {{first_name}},

The call takes about 30 minutes:

1. Where you are now: your trading, your challenges so far, what keeps going wrong.
2. What you want your trading to look like in a year.
3. How the mentorship works, what it costs, and whether it fits you.

If it isn't a fit, we'll tell you. No pressure either way.

Jay

preCallEmails.subject: Tomorrow: your call with Jay's team
preCallEmails.body:
Hey {{first_name}},

Quick reminder: your call is tomorrow at {{call_time}}.

If the time doesn't work anymore, reschedule with the link in your invite so someone else can take the slot.

See you tomorrow,
Jay

preCallEmails.subject: Today's the day
preCallEmails.body:
Hey {{first_name}},

Your call is today at {{call_time}}. Find a quiet spot and have your questions ready.

One day. One trade at a time.
Jay
